intro: Tools for making models smaller and comparing their cost and answers. Explore RTX 5080 experiments through individual records and the code behind them. No GPU needed.
c7title: Select groups. Slice the MLP. Check unseen inputs.
c7intro: INDEPENDENT scores channel groups separately; PAIRWISE also considers how their output changes cancel or reinforce each other. Both remove channels from one Qwen3-0.6B MLP calculation block. B is the original 16-bit floating-point (BF16) baseline.
c6title: Follow answer scores through a one-layer intervention.
c6intro: B is the original 16-bit floating-point (BF16) model. A_PUBLIC and V4 replace the attention operation that selects and mixes input information in layer 13. Only the initial prompt processing (prefill) changes; weights and other layers remain BF16.
guide: Developer reproduction · CPU build and checks
scope: One model, one layer, synthetic tasks. Deployment: NOT_ASSESSED.
readoutNote: POST-HOC · SAME-INPUT READOUT DIAGNOSTIC. FP32 recomputes the final vocabulary projection from the same hidden states and represented BF16 weights. These are reused scenarios, not new samples or a live model setting.
nativeNote: ORIGINAL NATIVE OUTPUT. Choice accuracy uses four allowed labels. A flip may be a gain, a regression, or a different wrong answer. Standard and baseline-selected stress are separate sets.
c7note: 25% deletion slightly reduced local error with PAIRWISE; at 50% both selectors chose the same groups. Lower reconstruction error and closer baseline choices did not yield the best gold NLL. COMPLETED_NO_CLEAR_TRANSFER.
c6limits: Native standard: 5/192 A_PUBLIC flips, 8/192 V4 flips; no regressions. Selected stress: 2/46 and 1/46 regressions. B code accuracy was 15/64; strict structured generation was 0/24 for each arm.
c7limits: Local errors use 32 fixed positions at length 512. Gold is the independently computed correct answer. NLL is negative log probability of that choice; lower is better. Δ means candidate minus B.
empty: No matching inputs. Reset filters or change the ID.
invalid: Invalid link filter. Reset to the full dataset.
guided: Guided examples (fixed first ID per task)
top: Options with exactly equal highest scores
mass: Total probability assigned to the four options
logits: Four option scores before probability conversion (logits)
local: Relative output error in the changed operation (%)
costNote7: Timing covers 6 fixed inputs in separate paired rounds, not the displayed item. Speedup = B time / candidate time. Local MLP and whole-model prefill are separate; all model-prefill intervals include 1. Memory includes co-resident comparison modules.
costNote6: Recorded model-prefill ratios refer to the original native study, not the FP32 head diagnostic. A_PUBLIC ≈1.004×; V4 ≈1.001×. They do not inherit Case004/005 operator speedups.
evidence: Code and record version behind the evidence (revision)
presentation: File-content check value for the display source (fingerprint)
foot: Qwen / Transformers and upstream kernels supply the model operations. This project supplies comparison, structural surgery and evidence tools, with OpenAI Codex assistance. Apache-2.0 project code; upstream terms remain applicable.
tieHelp: Exact ties use stored numeric equality; first label wins. A tie-involved flip remains part of the native result. FP32 is a separate same-input sensitivity view.
probHelp: Probabilities are conditional on the four labels. Allowed-label mass shows how much full-vocabulary probability those labels receive. Full KL is a retained full-vector scalar; four logits cannot reconstruct it.
localHelp: Case007: MLP reconstruction versus the original module, pooled fixed tokens. Case006: candidate attention versus native BF16, pooled fixed queries. Different denominators; not a shared error scale.
noData: The display data is missing or malformed. Rebuild with tools/showcase/build.py; no example results were substituted.
tieHelp7: Exact top sets use stored score equality and the original first-label tie break.
guide_intro: This developer guide builds the static viewer and checks public records on CPU. Use the model guides for settings and failures, and the measurement guide for interpreting numbers. Use a compatible environment with Python 3.12.14 and NumPy 2.3.5 and a new external output directory. No model or GPU is loaded.
guide_result: The 4/16 selections are INDEPENDENT [8,12,13,14] and PAIRWISE [8,13,14,15]. Both 8/16 selections are [7,8,9,11,12,13,14,15]. Each matches the preserved selection. Evaluating 1,820/12,870 objectives is CPU arithmetic, not that many model runs.
guide_browser: Open the completed HTML directly with file://. Browser check code and environment notes are in presentation/README.md in the repository. Desktop viewport emulation is separate from physical-device testing. The full reproduction notes below distinguish public-record checks from GPU reruns and their prerequisites.

homeTitle7: From channel selection to a smaller model block
homeIntro7: Built a selector and weight-slicing adapter that turn chosen channel groups into a smaller MLP, a block that transforms information inside the model.
homeIntro6: Built a one-layer attention adapter and paired tools for comparing answer probabilities, choice transitions and exact top-score ties.
homeLimit7: A small local reduction at 25%; the same groups at 50%. Closer baseline fidelity did not yield the best gold NLL. Whole-model prefill speedup was not established.

homeIntro: DIOVA builds tools to compress, save and reload models, then compare their outputs and execution costs. Explore the PyTorch implementations, RTX 5080 measurements and browser-based results.
homeKicker: Model compression · GPU measurement · Answer comparison
projectResult7: Local error decreased slightly at 25% removal; both methods chose the same structure at 50%. The smaller one-layer MLP ran faster, while whole-model prefill speedup was not established. Closer baseline fidelity did not yield the best probability score for the correct answer.
projectResult6: The records separate standard-set choice changes from selected stress results. The follow-up on final vocabulary-score precision is a post-hoc diagnostic on the same inputs.

cap1Title: Save smaller models and run them again
cap1Body: Applied GPTQ quantization, which stores weights with fewer bits, and connected the files to an inference engine. Built a loader that checks and restores models whose MLP widths differ by layer.
cap2Title: Measure GPU costs and changed answers
cap2Body: Implemented runners that compare response time, GPU memory and answer scores on the same questions. Individual operations and complete model requests are timed separately.
cap3Title: Recalculate records and make results inspectable
cap3Body: Implemented Python tools that recalculate saved measurements and web interfaces that compare answers question by question. Automated checks connect displayed values to the source records.
cap3Tech: Python · JavaScript · GitHub Actions · GitHub Pages

stack3Body: Fit output weights for a smaller MLP block, select channel groups for deletion, and compare results paired by question.

homeIntro8: Build GPTQ checkpoints and connect them to the inference engine. Save and restore models with layer-specific MLP widths, and fit the output weights of a smaller module.

homeHeroTitle: Store smaller AI models, run them, and check which answers and tasks changed.
homeHeroSubtitle: DIOVA is a portfolio of tools I implemented to convert, save, measure and evaluate public AI models during inference: running a trained model to produce answers.
homeOutcomeIntro: The implementations and measurements use Qwen models and an RTX 5080 graphics card (GPU) with 16GB of memory. They relate to model deployment tooling, inference performance measurement and quality checks after model changes.
outputTitle8: Check that a smaller saved model can run again
outputIntro8: Implemented tools to reduce one model’s weight-file size and to reduce output error in another model after channel removal. The two models and their results are presented separately.
outputQTitle: From compressed weights to execution in a fresh process
outputQBody: Built a pipeline that converts Qwen to 4-bit weights with 16-bit inputs (GPTQ W4A16), checks the saved weights and settings, copies the files, and runs them in a fresh vLLM process.
outputQMetric: Weight files · Original BF16 → GPTQ W4A16 · Decimal GB
outputRTitle: Restore a smaller structure and reduce its output error
outputRBody: Fit and save output weights in a fixed smaller MLP using ridge regression. The loader builds an empty matching model structure (meta skeleton) from saved layer sizes and checks that structure and weights match before reloading (strict reload), without the original checkpoint.
outputRMetric: Reduction in deletion-induced local squared output error
outputRScope: Qwen3-0.6B · One MLP layer · BF16 · Reconstruction evaluated on 192 short synthetic held-out prompts
outputTitle7: Choose which channels to remove, then shrink the matrices
outputBody7: Implemented tools that score channel groups in a model’s MLP block individually or together. They slice matching weight matrices into smaller PyTorch modules and check their computation against the original module with the same channels masked.
outputScope7: Qwen3-0.6B · One MLP layer · 16 channel groups
outputTitle6: Find which answers change after a model calculation changes
outputBody6: Replaced one attention operation, which selects and mixes information from the input. Built tools that compare probabilities, choices and ties on the same questions, exposing answer changes hidden by aggregate scores.
outputStages6: Lost correct answers|New correct answers|Wrong-to-wrong changes
outputScope6: Qwen3-0.6B · One attention layer · Fixed synthetic questions
